practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was appointed as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, which was set up on August 29, 1947, to prepare a draft of the new Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: How many members were there in the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly, including the Chairman?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Drafting Committee had seven members: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (Chairman), N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, Dr. K.M. Munshi, Mohammad Saadulla, N. Madhava Rau, and T.T. Krishnamachari.

practiceQuestions.q: Who headed the Union Powers Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru headed both the Union Powers Committee and the Union Constitution Committee of the Constituent Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Provincial Constitution Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel headed the Provincial Constitution Committee as well as the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas.

practiceQuestions.q: Which committee was headed by Dr. Rajendra Prasad in the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. Rajendra Prasad headed the Steering Committee, the Ad Hoc Committee on the National Flag, and the Rules of Procedure Committee.

practiceQuestions.q: The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas had several sub-committees. Who headed the Sub-Committee on Fundamental Rights?
practiceQuestions.sol: Acharya J.B. Kripalani headed the Sub-Committee on Fundamental Rights, which operated under the Advisory Committee headed by Sardar Patel.

practiceQuestions.q: Who headed the Minorities Sub-Committee under the Advisory Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: H.C. Mukherjee was the Chairman of the Minorities Sub-Committee, which functioned under the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights and Minorities.

practiceQuestions.q: When was the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly set up?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Drafting Committee was established on August 29, 1947, entrusted with the responsibility of preparing a draft Constitution of India.

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following replaced B.L. Mitter in the Drafting Committee due to the latter's ill health?
practiceQuestions.sol: B.L. Mitter resigned from the Drafting Committee due to ill health, and N. Madhava Rau was appointed in his place.

practiceQuestions.q: Who replaced D.P. Khaitan in the Drafting Committee following his death in 1948?
practiceQuestions.sol: D.P. Khaitan passed away in 1948, and T.T. Krishnamachari was chosen to replace him on the Drafting Committee.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas considered unique and exceptionally significant among the committees of the Constituent Assembly?
opts: It was the only committee chaired directly by the Viceroy.
It had comprehensive scope and spawned several crucial sub-committees to deal with sensitive socio-political safeguards.
It was solely responsible for drafting the entire Constitution without any other committees.
It functioned independently of the Constituent Assembly plenary sessions.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Advisory Committee under Sardar Patel was overarching, dealing with complex questions of fundamental rights, religious minorities, and excluded tribal regions, necessitating dedicated sub-committees for each domain.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the structural relationship between the major committees (like the Union Powers and Union Constitution committees) and the Drafting Committee?
opts: The Drafting Committee acted in isolation, overriding recommendations made by all other committees.
The major committees laid down basic principles and policies, which were then synthesized and incorporated into a formal legal text by the Drafting Committee.
The Drafting Committee reported to the Provincial Committee rather than the plenary Constituent Assembly.
The Drafting Committee preceded all committees and dictated their mandates.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly first debated and approved broad principles and reports submitted by various committees (Union Powers, Provincial Constitution, etc.), and the Drafting Committee's primary role was to translate these into precise legal clauses for the draft Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Committee on the Rules of Procedure influence the functioning of the Constituent Assembly?
opts: It regulated internal proceedings, debates, voting mechanisms, and management of business in the Assembly.
It determined the administrative boundaries of newly integrated princely states.
It exclusively handled financial allocations for constitution-making.
It drafted civil and criminal codes for independent India.
practiceQuestions.sol: Chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the Committee on the Rules of Procedure framed the procedural guidelines to ensure orderly debate, deliberation, and decision-making within the Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary focus of the North-East Frontier Tribal Areas and Assam Excluded & Partially Excluded Areas Sub-Committee?
opts: To integrate French and Portuguese colonial enclaves into India.
To safeguard indigenous tribal cultures, land rights, and autonomy, later manifesting as the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution.
To establish defence pacts with neighbouring Himalayan kingdoms.
To administer revenue collection in the princely states of Rajputana.
practiceQuestions.sol: Chaired by Gopinath Bordoloi, this sub-committee examined the administrative needs of North-East tribal areas, leading to special governance mechanisms incorporated into the Sixth Schedule.

practiceQuestions.q: Why were both major and minor committees necessary alongside the plenary sessions of the Constituent Assembly?
opts: Plenary sessions lacked the legal quorum required to pass laws.
Specialized committees allowed for deep-dive technical research, negotiation, and consensus-building on complex issues before presenting them to the full assembly.
British colonial authorities mandated committee-based deliberations by law.
Members of the Constituent Assembly refused to meet in large gatherings.
practiceQuestions.sol: Constitution-making involved intricate legal, financial, and socio-political negotiations. Committees functioned as specialized working groups to iron out differences and produce vetted drafts for assembly-wide debate.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Ad Hoc Committee on the National Flag differ in nature from structural committees like the Union Constitution Committee?
opts: It was temporary and constituted for a specific symbolic/ceremonial task rather than permanent institutional design.
It had statutory veto power over all constitutional amendments.
It was appointed directly by the British Cabinet Mission.
It functioned exclusively after the Constitution was officially promulgated.
practiceQuestions.sol: An ad hoc committee is formed for a specific, time-bound purpose. The Flag Committee was tasked solely with designing and recommending India's national flag, unlike committees drafting organs of the state.

practiceQuestions.q: What constitutional significance does the Drafting Committee's meticulous scrutiny of amendments hold in India's constitutional history?
opts: It ensured that thousands of amendments proposed during Assembly debates were systematically debated, refined, and integrated without creating internal legal contradictions.
It allowed the Chairman to unilaterally rewrite fundamental rights without assembly approval.
It gave princely states absolute immunity from federal taxation.
It converted India from a parliamentary system to a presidential republic.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Drafting Committee reviewed every clause and amendment proposed by Assembly members, ensuring legal coherence, precision, and alignment with the overarching vision of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was a separate 'States Committee' (Committee for Negotiating with States) formed by the Constituent Assembly?
opts: To negotiate terms of accession and representation for princely states entering the Indian Union.
To handle trade agreements with British Dominions.
To demarcate boundaries between British India provinces.
To manage foreign exchange reserves during partition.
practiceQuestions.sol: The States Committee, headed by Jawaharlal Nehru, was tasked with negotiating with the princely states to bring them into the Constituent Assembly framework and the larger Indian Union.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Committee on Chief Commissioners' Provinces contribute to the federal structure designed by the Constituent Assembly?
opts: It recommended governance frameworks for territories directly administered by the Central Government (Union Territories).
It governed agricultural land reforms in northern provinces.
It oversaw military cantonments and railway security.
It managed the division of assets between India and Pakistan.
practiceQuestions.sol: Chief Commissioners' Provinces (like Delhi, Ajmer-Merwara, Coorg) were centrally administered areas. This committee examined how these regions should be governed under the new constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of having overlapping chairmanships among major committees (e.g., Nehru heading both Union Powers and Union Constitution committees)?
opts: It ensured ideological consistency, seamless coordination, and integration of core governance principles across different facets of the Constitution.
It concentrated dictatorial powers in a single individual, bypassing democratic debate.
It was done due to an acute shortage of literate members in the Assembly.
It was mandated by the British Crown to limit native representation.
practiceQuestions.sol: Key leaders like Nehru and Patel heading multiple related committees ensured that the philosophy underlying union powers matched the union constitution and provincial relations, avoiding conflicting provisions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly:
1. It was set up on August 29, 1947, to prepare a draft of the new Constitution.
2. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was assisted by six other members, including constitutional experts like Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar and K.M. Munshi.
3. The committee completed and submitted the entire Constitution to the Assembly in a single sitting without any revisions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Drafting Committee published the first draft in February 1948, invited public/assembly feedback, debated thousands of amendments, and went through multiple rigorous readings before final adoption.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following committees and their respective chairpersons in the Constituent Assembly:
1. Union Powers Committee – Jawaharlal Nehru
2. Provincial Constitution Committee – Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
3. Steering Committee – Dr. Rajendra Prasad
4. Committee on Fundamental Rights – J.B. Kripalani (Sub-committee level)
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
practiceQuestions.sol: All pairs are correctly matched. Nehru chaired the Union Powers Committee, Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee, Dr. Prasad chaired the Steering Committee, and Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee under the Advisory Committee.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas:
1. It was headed by Jawaharlal Nehru.
2. It included several sub-committees under its umbrella, such as the North-East Frontier Tribal Areas Sub-Committee and the Excluded and Partially Excluded Areas Sub-Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Advisory Committee was headed by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, not Jawaharlal Nehru. Statement 2 is correct; it had multiple sub-committees including those for tribal and excluded areas.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the major and minor committees of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The Union Constitution Committee and the Provincial Constitution Committee were both headed by the same person.
2. The Committee on Financial Relations between the Union and the States was a major committee of the Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false because the Union Constitution Committee was headed by Nehru, while the Provincial Constitution Committee was headed by Patel. Statement 2 is false as financial relations were dealt with under specific expert bodies/provisions rather than being a major standalone committee of that exact nomenclature in the primary list.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Drafting Committee members:
1. N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar and Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar were prominent jurists included in the Drafting Committee.
2. T.T. Krishnamachari was an original founding member of the Drafting Committee appointed in August 1947.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Ayyangar and Ayyar were key legal experts on the committee. Statement 2 is incorrect because T.T. Krishnamachari joined later to replace D.P. Khaitan after Khaitan's death in 1948.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functioning of Constituent Assembly committees:
1. All committees submitted their final reports directly to the British Parliament for enactment.
2. The Constituent Assembly appointed a total of eight major committees along with several minor committees and sub-committees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because committees submitted their reports to the Constituent Assembly itself, not the British Parliament. Statement 2 is correct; the Assembly appointed 8 major committees and numerous minor/sub-committees.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly:
1. It was chaired by G.V. Mavalankar.
2. It was established to deal with the dual role of the Assembly as a constitution-making body and a provisional parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. G.V. Mavalankar chaired the Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly, which addressed the administrative and procedural bifurcation when the Assembly functioned as the Dominion Legislature/Parliament vs. Constituent body.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements concerning the Drafting Committee:
1. It was the most crucial committee entrusted with the task of preparing the Constitution of India.
2. Its chairman, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, was elected to the Constituent Assembly from the Bengal province initially.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Drafting Committee was indeed the most pivotal body. Dr. Ambedkar was initially elected from East Bengal, but following partition, that seat went to Pakistan, and he was subsequently re-elected from Bombay province (Pune seat vacated by M.R. Jayakar).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Order Business Committee of the Constituent Assembly:
1. It was responsible for managing the day-to-day legislative calendar and business schedule of the Constituent Assembly.
2. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as the chairman of the Order Business Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. The 'Order of Business Committee' was headed by Dr. K.M. Munshi (or Dr. Rajendra Prasad / K.M. Munshi in various procedural contexts, but notably not Dr. Ambedkar, and its scope was distinct from daily legislative calendering which fell under general steering/functions frameworks).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the expert committees appointed outside or alongside the Constituent Assembly committees:
1. The Expert Committee on the Financial Provisions of the Union Constitution was headed by Nalini Ranjan Sarkar.
2. The Constituent Assembly did not seek any external expert opinions and relied solely on its 389 members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; the Expert Committee on Financial Provisions was headed by N.R. Sarkar. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Assembly appointed various expert committees and consulted outside legal luminaries (like B.N. Rau who prepared the initial draft as constitutional advisor).
